newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jailed ex-Cannes mayor in fresh sleaze probe.
newsitem.headline: Jailed ex-Cannes mayor in fresh sleaze probe.

text.p: The detained ex-mayor of the French Riviera resort of Cannes, Michel Mouillot, faced a fresh corruption probe on Thursday on suspicion of illicitly receiving corporate funds.

Justice sources said a judge questioned Mouillot for six hours and ordered him to be formally investigated on suspicion of corruption, influence-peddling, misusing corporate funds and falsifying documents.
They said he was suspected of illicitly receiving funds through a subsidiary of water utility Compagnie Generale des Eaux.
Investigators said more than 10 million francs ($1.7 million) was channeled to Mouillot through the Phenix real estate firm, which was then headed by a Mouillot associate, Jean-Marc Oury.
An aide to Oury, Jean-Francois Bourdaloue, was formally placed under investigation on Wednesday for suspected corruption in the same case.

The investigation started when co-owners of part of the Croisette seafront boulevard appealed to magistrates against the town hall which wanted to expropriate them to build a hotel complex near the Palm Beach casino.
They accused Mouillot, a centre-right politician once dubbed the "Kennedy of the Croisette", of "distorting a public procedure for the benefit of private interests."
Mouillot has been in pre-trial custody since July in connection with two other cases in which he is accused of soliciting bribes in exchange for permits to install one-arm bandits in casinos.
He resigned as mayor last month after the Supreme Court threw out an appeal against a previous conviction for corruption.
He was barred from holding public office for five years as part of an 18-month suspended prison sentence and 200,000 franc ($40,000) fine for receiving a ficticious salary from a Lyon businessman.
